hz.auto_tip:
Auto gates: a note that holds still gets Fixed gates when they're off
its tone by at most this many cents, else Alternating ones (0 to {most}).
About 5 cents is where most ears start to hear it.
Right-click a note to give it a threshold of its own.
hz.auto_shared: Use the Hz bass's threshold ({cents} cents)
hz.auto_shared_one: Use the Hz bass's threshold ({cents} cent)
hz.auto_ask:
Auto gates threshold of this note in cents, from 0 to {most}.
Fixed gates when they're off by at most this much, else Alternating.
With several selected, they all move by as much, each from its own value.
Drag the box sideways to try values.
hz.step_auto: Hz bass: a note's Auto threshold
hz.auto_fixed: Auto: Fixed gates (off by {off} cents, threshold {limit})
hz.auto_mixed: Auto: Alternating gates (Fixed would be off by {off} cents, threshold {limit})
hz.own_fixed: Fixed gates, this note's own (off by {off} cents)
hz.own_mixed: Alternating gates, this note's own (Fixed would be off by {off} cents)
hz.name: Hz bass
hz.grow_tip:
Ticked: the shape on the piano roll is made as long as the notes here.
Not ticked: the shape keeps its length, and notes past its end (the grey part) aren't used.
hz.bend_tip:
Gives a note its own bend: click a note to add a point to its bend line and drag it up or down.
The line stretches with the note and is heard on top of everything else, up to the Pitch box's Range.
Points snap to the grid and to whole keys (Shift: free). Right-click a point to remove it.
Drag the small square between two points up or down to curve that piece; double-click it to make it straight.
Right-click a note's bend line for the note's menu.
On empty space it works like the Select tool (box, Ctrl+box adds, a click unselects).
hz.step_note_bend_delete: Hz bass: remove a bend point
hz.bend_copied: Bend copied: right-click another note → Bend → Paste bend.
hz.pencil_tip:
Press on empty space to place a note. Ctrl+drag selects with a box.
Double right-click switches between Select and Pencil.
hz.select_tip:
Drag on empty space to select the notes the box touches (Ctrl: add to the selected ones; Shift: no snap).
Notes can still be moved and resized. Double right-click switches between Select and Pencil.
hz.ppq_tip:
The PPQ of the whole project (the same box as under Project).
A higher PPQ brings the red line closer to the exact tone.
hz.fx_tip:
Shows or hides the effects pane under the notes.
Effects that are on keep working while it's hidden.
hz.line_tip:
Ticked: the red line shows the tone you hear (the middle of a row = the exact tone).
The faint line behind it is each repeat's own pitch.
Zoomed in, drag it up or down to tune a note (double-click: back to 0). The dots of a slide can be dragged.
Not ticked: the line and its dots are hidden. Slides and tunes that were made stay.
hz.hint_none: Select a Hz bass to change its notes, or pick the Hz bass tool (H) and drag on the piano roll where a new one should start. To give a spam shape Hz bass notes, select it and press Notes… in the side panel.
hz.hint_none_short: Select a Hz bass, or drag with the Hz bass tool (H) to start one.
hz.hint_new: New Hz bass starting at beat {beat}: click to place its first note.
hz.stale: BPM changed: this Hz bass is out of tune.
hz.cc_shared_tip: In the MIDI file, this Hz bass's channel also plays: {names}. A CC changes everything on its channel, so its CC lines change them too. To keep them apart, pick Multi channel with "Split: any notes at the same time".
hz.cc_play: CC reaches other notes while playing
hz.cc_play_tip: While playing in Spiderweb, this MIDI out has only 16 channels, so this Hz bass shares a channel with: {names}. Its CC lines change them too. Built-in BASSMIDI has enough channels to keep them apart. The MIDI file isn't affected.
hz.cc_play_own_tip: While playing in Spiderweb, this MIDI out has only 16 channels, so this Hz bass's own channels per note wrap round and its notes hear each other's CC lines. Built-in BASSMIDI has enough channels. The MIDI file isn't affected.
hz.clash_tip: Two layers sound the same key at the same time. One channel can't play a key twice at once, so the notes of the lower layer in the list go on another channel. Move a note in time or to another key to keep them on one channel.
hz.undo_elsewhere: The last change was made on the piano roll: undo it there.
hz.redo_elsewhere: The next change to redo was made on the piano roll: redo it there.
hz.tool_curve_tip:
Drag (or click, then click again) to draw a curve, then bend it with its handles (Alt: a sharp corner). Middle-click on it adds a point; right-click on a point removes it.
It becomes notes joined by slides that follow it. Faint notes show what it will make; Enter or a right-click elsewhere makes them, Esc throws it away.
Its points snap to the grid and to whole keys (Shift: free).
hz.tool_arc_tip:
Click the start, a point it passes through, then the end (or drag from start to end, then click where it passes through) to draw a piece of a circle.
It becomes notes joined by slides that follow it. Faint notes show what it will make; drag its points to change it. Enter or a right-click makes the notes, Esc throws it away.
Its points snap to the grid and to whole keys (Shift: free).
hz.tool_poly_tip:
Click each point (or drag each piece) to draw a polyline; double-click ends it. It becomes notes joined by slides, so the tone glides along it.
Faint notes show what it will make. Drag its points to change it; Enter or a right-click makes the notes, Esc throws it away.
Its points snap to the grid and to whole keys (Shift: free). Each point comes after the one before it in time.
hz.tool_free_tip:
Drag to draw freely: the tone follows your line, with as few notes and slides as fit it.
Faint notes show what it will make; Enter or a right-click makes them, Esc throws it away.
It never snaps. Going back to the left changes the pitch at the same moment.
hz.tool_line_tip:
Drag (or click, then click again) to draw a line: it becomes notes joined by a slide, so the tone glides along it.
Faint notes show what it will make. Drag its ends to change it; Enter or a right-click makes the notes, Esc throws it away.
Its ends snap to the grid and to whole keys (Shift: free).
hz.domino_bad: Couldn't read the notes copied in Domino: {e}
hz.domino_left_out_one: — 1 more track left out (a Hz bass has {most} layers at most)
hz.domino_left_out: — {n} more tracks left out (a Hz bass has {most} layers at most)
hz.tune_ask:
Tune of this note in cents (100 = one key), from -{most} to {most}.
0 = the exact tone.
With several selected, they all move by as much, each from its own value.
Drag the box sideways to try values.
hz.fx_slant_tip: Slant: every key starts a little later than the key below it. 100 % = spread over one whole wave. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_groups_tip: Groups: the keys take turns in groups. 0 % = all together, 20 % = 2 groups, up to 6 groups at 100 %. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_offpitch_tip: Off pitch: every key repeats a little slower or faster than the tone, so the keys drift apart and meet again by themselves. 100 % = 2 % between the lowest and the highest key. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_noisy_tip: Noisy: every repeat is late by a random bit. 100 % = up to one whole wave. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_height_tip: Height: the drawn wave shape (Hz shape…) gets taller or shorter. 100 % = as drawn, lower = keys it no longer reaches go quiet, higher (up to 400 %) = it grows past the Hz bass onto the keys above and below. Right-click → Repeat every + Shape → Sine for a shape that grows and shrinks. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_height_rand_tip: Random height: every wave gets its own height, a random bit taller or shorter than Height says (the same for all keys). 100 % = anywhere from flat to twice as tall, but never past 400 %. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_volume_tip: Volume: how loud. 100 % = the shape's own velocity, 0 % = silence (no notes there). Right-click → Repeat every + Shape → Pump for a pumping bass. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_sweep_tip: Sweep: a bump of loudness that travels over the keys. 0 % = the lowest keys are loud, 100 % = the highest. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_wah_tip: Wah: loud and quiet stripes over the keys, more stripes the higher the line (0 % = every key full). Strongest together with Slant. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_tremolo_tip: Tremolo: louder and quieter in turn. The line is how fast: 0 % = steady, 100 % = 8 times a beat (how much quieter: the synth window's Depth knob). Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_octave_tip: Octave below: every other repeat is softer, so the tone an octave below comes in. 100 % = as soft as it goes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_vibrato_tip: Vibrato: the tone itself goes a little up and down, 5 times every two beats (or as the synth window's Rate knob says). 100 % = 5 % of its pitch each way. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_pitch_tip: Pitch: bends the tone up or down. 50 % = as placed, 100 % = Range keys up, 0 % = Range keys down (the Pitch box's Range in the synth window, 12 to start with). Points stick to whole keys (hold Shift for in between). With Repeat every: a wobble; Once per note: a drop or rise at each note. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_sine_tip: Sine: every key hits 16 times in each wave, loud then soft like a sine wave. It takes the overtones away: a soft, pure tone. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_square_tip: Square: every key hits through half of each wave and rests through the other half. It takes every second overtone away: a hollow tone. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_saw_tip: Saw: every key hits 16 times in each wave, softer and softer. It makes the high overtones a little quieter. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_triangle_tip: Triangle: every key hits 16 times in each wave, louder, then softer. It takes every second overtone away and softens the rest. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_cc_head_tip: The lines under here make no notes: they're saved as MIDI messages (CC) on the channel the Hz bass's notes are on, and the player changes the sound with them. They change EVERYTHING on that channel. Each player reads them its own way. When the lines end, the channel goes back to how players start it.
hz.fx_cc_cutoff_tip: Cutoff (CC 74): makes the sound darker, like a synth's filter. 64 (the middle) = as it is; lower = darker. Most players only make it darker, not brighter. With Repeat every: the classic wobble. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_cc_expression_tip: Expression (CC 11): how loud, in dB. The top = as loud as the notes are; the bottom = silent. Unlike quieter notes, the sound keeps its brightness. A limiter hides a fade while the sound is too loud. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_cc_volume_tip: Channel volume (CC 7): how loud the whole channel is, in dB. Players start at -4 dB (100), so the top is a little louder than no line; the bottom = silent at once, the ring too. A limiter hides a fade while the sound is too loud. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_cc_pan_tip: Pan (CC 10): left or right. The middle = both sides. Some players turn one side fully off, others only a little. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_cc_wheel_tip: Pitch wheel (pitch bend): bends what the player plays up or down, up to 12 keys. The Hz bass's tone stays: it makes the sound brighter going up and darker going down. Points stick to whole keys (hold Shift for in between). Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_hint: Click an effect on the left to put it on: one line over all the notes. Drag its points, press on the line for a new point.
hz.fx_bend_tip: Drag up or down to bend this line. Double-click: straight again.
hz.fx_hold: Hold (a step at the next point)
hz.fx_sustain: Sustain here until the note ends
hz.fx_sustain_needs: Sustain here (needs Plays: Once per note, not stretched)
hz.fx_sustain_tip: Sustain point: the line stays here while the note lasts, and the rest plays after the note ends.
hz.fx_repeats_sustain: It stays at its sustain point until the note ends, then plays the rest.
hz.fx_bypass: Bypass (switch it off, keep its line)
hz.fx_is_off: It's switched off (Bypass): click its small square to switch it on again.
hz.fx_box_tip: Click the small square to switch it off without losing its line (Bypass).
hz.fx_amount: Amount line (how strong the repeat is)
hz.fx_repeat_off: Stop repeating (one line over all the notes)
hz.fx_repeats_note: It plays once from each note's start, {every} long.
hz.fx_repeats_restart: It repeats every {every}, starting over at each note.
hz.fx_repeats_note_fit: It plays once over each note, stretched to the note.
hz.fx_repeats_restart_fit: It starts over at each note, stretched to the note.
hz.fx_shape_drop_pitch: Drop (12 keys up, falling to the tone)
hz.fx_shape_rise_pitch: Rise (12 keys down, rising to the tone)
hz.loud_tip:
Shows or hides the loudness pane under the notes.
Each note's line sets its velocity; the layer's line turns the whole layer up and down, like a mixer's fader. The two multiply.
hz.loud_notes_tip:
Draw each note's own loudness line, in velocity (1 to 127). It takes the place of the Hz bass's velocity for that note.
A note without a line (dotted) takes the Hz bass's velocity. When notes are selected, only they change.
hz.loud_layer_tip:
Draw the loudness line of the layer picked, from 0 to 100 %. It turns every note of the layer down, after the effects, like a mixer's fader (0 % = silence).
Dotted at 100 % until drawn.
hz.loud_hint: Ctrl = flat line, Shift = snap to the grid, Enter = done
hz.loud_clear_notes: Back to the Hz bass's velocity
hz.layers_btn_tip:
Shows or hides the layers list on the left.
Each layer has its own notes and its own sound, like a track. Click a layer to change its notes and sound; the other layers' notes show faded.
hz.layers_none: No Hz bass yet: place a note first.
hz.layer_add_tip: Adds a new empty layer and picks it.
hz.slide_remove: Remove the slide between the selected notes
hz.arp_slides: Arpeggio on: slides are left out (they come back when it's off)
hz.slide_start: Start a slide here (then right-click another note)
synth.no_dll: The built-in synth couldn't start (its BASS files are missing or don't fit this Python): {err}
synth.pack_codec: The soundfont "{name}" couldn't be read: it's packed in a format the built-in synth can't play.
synth.sfz_spaced: The soundfont "{name}" couldn't be read: it has "sample =" with a space before "=", which the built-in synth can't handle. Open the .sfz file in a text editor and remove that space.
synth.bad_font_files:
The soundfont "{name}" couldn't be read: the files it needs are missing or can't be read.

{files}
synth.silent: Some sounds of the soundfont "{name}" will be missing: {n} files it needs are missing or can't be read.
synth.silent_one: Some sounds of the soundfont "{name}" will be missing: 1 file it needs is missing or can't be read.
synth.silent_why:
Missing: the file isn't where the soundfont says (moved or renamed?).
Can't be read: a sound format the built-in synth can't play (Opus, for example). WAV, OGG and MP3 work.
synth.failed: The built-in synth couldn't make the sound (BASS error {err}).
hz.preview_tip:
Hear this Hz bass alone through the built-in synth, with your soundfont.
Grey over the notes = sound not made yet; it clears as it's made (about a minute ahead of the play line, or of the left edge of the view).
Space = play / stop. Click the bar numbers to move the play line.
The first time, it asks for a soundfont (.sf2 / .sfz).
hz.preview_pick_font: Pick a soundfont for the preview
hz.bpm_needed: The BPM box needs a number (4 to 100000) first: the tone is worked out from it.
synth.no_device: There's no sound device to play through.
hz.settings_tip: The Hz bass's Pitch, Gates and PPQ, whether the shape grows with the notes, Hz shape… (how the notes look inside a wave and how long they last), and the preview's soundfont, voice limit, reverb and volume.
ps.title: Hz bass settings
ps.change_tip: Pick another soundfont (.sf2 / .sfz). The sound is made again with it.
ps.voices_tip:
How many sounds can ring at once. More = fuller and closer to a big render, but slower to make.
Change it and the notes grey again while the sound is made anew: watch the speed below.
ps.nofx_tip: Ticked: the soundfont's reverb and chorus are left out (a drier, clearer sound).
ps.off: The preview is off (the Preview button in the Hz bass window).
ps.full: full: the oldest sounds are cut short
ps.speed: Speed: {speed}x real time ({n} pieces at once)
ps.speed_one: Speed: {speed}x real time ({n} piece at a time)
ps.slow: slower than playing: playing waits at the grey
ps.limiter: A limiter always keeps the sound from getting too loud, however many keys play at once.
ps.live_mb_tip: How much memory the live keys may keep for the notes they record from the soundfont. When it's full, the ones used least are thrown away and recorded again when needed (a short wait). All of them are freed a minute after the synth window closes.
ps.live_used: Live keys: {used} MB of {limit} MB kept
hz.live_needs_preview: Turn Preview on in the Hz bass window to play the keys live.
hz.trace_tip: How the notes look inside one wave: draw where the keys hit (a line through one wave, left to right, over the Hz bass's keys, bottom to top) and set how long each note lasts, with small previews at a few pitches. Same pitch, different texture.
hz.trace_reset_tip:
This layer back to the main line and Note length.
With one layer: line straight, Note length back to 100 % and the last note no longer sticking out.
hz.trace_hint: Drag points to change the shape, or the end of a bar to change the note length. Click the line to add a point, right-click one to remove it. Shift = off the grid. More in Help (F1).
hz.trace_strips_tip: How the notes look in the piano roll at a few pitches, from low (left) to high (right): the lowest, middle and highest notes of the Hz bass (a few octaves when it has none). Each shows the same stretch of time, so a higher pitch shows more waves. Effects aren't shown.
hz.trace_shapes_tip: Start from a ready-made shape or one you saved (newest first; type a letter while the list is open to jump to it). Straight and Saw hit each key once a wave; the other ready-made ones hit each key twice (twice the notes). Empty while the line is one of your own that isn't saved.
hz.trace_layer_tip: With layers, a line drawn here is for the layer picked only. Layers you haven't changed use the main line, and new layers start with it.
hz.trace_all_tip: This line becomes the main line and every layer uses it (no layer keeps a line of its own).
hz.trace_back_tip: This layer uses the main line again.
hz.trace_save_tip: Save the line drawn under a name. Saved lines show in the shapes box, under the ready-made ones, newest first.
hz.trace_delete_tip: Delete the saved shape picked in the shapes box (you're asked first). Ready-made shapes can't be deleted.
hz.trace_kept_bad: The old saved shapes file couldn't be read: it was kept as hz_shapes.json.bad.
hz.trace_built_in: "{name}" is a ready-made shape. Pick another name.
hz.step_wave_all: Hz bass: wave shape for all layers
hz.step_length_all: Hz bass: note length for all layers
hz.length_tip:
How long each repeat lasts. 100 % = until the next one starts (no gaps). Less = a gap after each one.
% of a wave: that much of one wave of the note's tone, so the notes follow the drawn wave shape on every pitch. A fraction works too: 1/8 = 12.5 %.
% of the note: that much of how long each note is now.
Ticks: every repeat that many ticks long.
Never longer than at 100 %. The pitch stays the same.
hz.length_layer_tip: With layers, a length typed here (or dragged in the drawing) is for the layer picked only. Layers you haven't changed use the main length, and new layers start with it.
hz.length_all_tip: This length becomes the main length and every layer uses it (no layer keeps a length of its own).
hz.length_back_tip: This layer uses the main length again.
hz.stick: Last note sticks out of the shape
hz.stick_tip:
Ticked: the last repeat before a gap or the end keeps a whole wave, even past the shape's end (it never reaches the next note on its key).
Not ticked: it's cut where the notes end.
hz.stick_funnel: Funnels keep every note inside their wall.
hz.step_stick: Hz bass: last note sticks out
hz.synth_tip: A window like a synth's: knobs for the sound, the effects' lines for one note, and a keyboard to hear the Hz bass live (a quick copy made from your soundfont, not your MIDI).
hz.synth_warning: What you hear here is a quick copy made from your soundfont, NOT your MIDI. Place notes in the Hz bass window to keep them.
hz.synth_hint: Click and hold a key below to hear it. These are the Hz bass window's own effects, shown for one note.
hz.synth_hint_knobs: Turn a knob, then click and hold a key below to hear it.
hz.synth_letters: Letters A to ; play {lo} to {hi} (Z / X: an octave down / up).
hz.synth_osc2_off: Off: click the name to switch it on
hz.synth_tip_osc2_on: Click to switch the second oscillator on or off. On (lit): every note you placed is played a second time by OSC B, with its own waveform and tune, on top of OSC A. Turning one of its knobs or picking one of its choices switches it on too. While it is on, OSC A's light switches OSC A's own notes on and off, so you can hear OSC B alone.
hz.synth_tip_osc2_wave: Waveform: the shape of OSC B's waves, apart from OSC A's. Plain = one note a wave. Sine, Square, Triangle and Saw make up to 16 notes a wave (see its Shape).
hz.synth_tip_osc2_shape: Shape: how much of OSC B's waveform is used. 0 % = the plain tone, 100 % = the whole waveform (more notes).
hz.synth_tip_osc2_octave: Octave: OSC B's tone this many octaves up or down from each note. One octave up = twice as many notes for OSC B.
hz.synth_tip_osc2_semi: Semi: OSC B's tone this many keys up or down (7 = a fifth up, 12 = an octave).
hz.synth_tip_osc2_fine: Fine: OSC B's tone a little up or down, in cents (100 = one key). A few cents off OSC A makes the two drift in and out of each other, a thicker sound.
hz.synth_tip_osc2_level: Level: how loud OSC B is next to OSC A. 0 % = silent (its notes left out).
hz.synth_tip_osc2_plays: Plays on: Every key = every key of the shape plays both OSC A and OSC B (about twice the notes). Split keys = the keys take turns, one playing OSC A, the next OSC B (no extra notes, but each oscillator has only half the keys).
hz.synth_tip_osc2_mode: OSC B's own Mode, apart from OSC A's.
hz.synth_tip_timing: Timing: how the Rate knob moves. Free = any speed. Straight = only note lengths, in step with the beat (1/4 = once a beat, 1/8 = twice…). Triplets = 3 in the time of 2 of those (1/8T = 3 times a beat). Dotted = one and a half times as long (1/8D). The note length shows beside the Rate.
hz.synth_tip_vibrato_wait: Delay: no vibrato for this long after each note starts, then it comes in (over Rise). 0 = right away.
hz.synth_tip_tremolo_wait: Delay: no tremolo for this long after each note starts, then it comes in (over Rise). 0 = right away.
hz.synth_tip_tremolo_rise: Rise: after the Delay, the tremolo grows from nothing to its full Depth over this long. 0 = full at once.
hz.synth_tip_mode: Mode: one more way to change the shape of each wave. FM = the wave is pushed back and forth by a fast wobble (a metal or bell-like sound). Pulse width = only the first part of each wave sounds (a hollow, nasal sound). Sync = the wave starts over faster inside each wave (a hard, screaming sound). Growl = every other wave lands a bit late, so a lower tone growls under it. Bitcrush = the notes are moved onto a coarse grid (rough and gritty). FM, Pulse width and Sync make up to 16 notes a wave; Growl and Bitcrush add none.
hz.synth_tip_fm_depth: Depth: how hard the wobble pushes the wave. 0 = no change. Works on the Waveform picked (with Plain it uses a sine).
hz.synth_tip_fm_ratio: Ratio: how fast the wobble is, times the note's tone. Whole numbers (1, 2, 3…) sound in tune; others sound like a bell or metal.
hz.synth_tip_fm_time: Time: the wobble dies away over this long after each note starts, so the note starts bright and settles (an FM bass pluck). 0 = it stays.
hz.synth_tip_pulse_width: Width: how much of each wave sounds. 50 % = a square wave, less = thinner and more nasal.
hz.synth_tip_pulse_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the width opens up to 50 % and back (the classic moving pulse sound). 0 = it stays still.
hz.synth_tip_sync_amount: Amount: how many times faster the wave starts over inside each wave of the note's tone. The note's tone stays the same; the colour changes a lot.
hz.synth_tip_sync_time: Time: the amount rises from 1 to its full value over this long after each note starts (the sweeping sync sound). 0 = full at once.
hz.synth_tip_growl_amount: Amount: how late every other wave lands. 100 % = half a wave. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_growl_every: Every: the late waves take turns over this many waves: 2 = a tone an octave lower comes in, 3 = lower still.
hz.synth_tip_crush_amount: Amount: how coarse the grid the notes are moved onto is. The more, the rougher. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tab_knobs_tip: OSC: the sound's main settings (wave, volume, pitch, LFOs, tone, voices, arpeggio).
hz.synth_tab_effects_tip: The effects on the sound: Chorus, Flanger, Echo, Reverb and Compressor look-alikes.
hz.synth_macro_hint: Drag a macro's name onto a knob, hold it there until the knob lights up, then let go to link them. Drag the coloured ring round a linked knob to set how far the macro turns it.
hz.synth_tip_macro: A macro turns every knob linked to it at once. Each linked knob keeps its own setting and the macro adds to it: at 100 % the knob gets as far as its coloured ring shows. A macro is one setting for the whole sound (it doesn't move during a note).
hz.synth_tip_macro_name:
Drag this name onto any knob on the OSC or FX tab and hold it there until the knob lights up (half a second), then let go: the knob is linked to this macro.
Click: pick this macro (the knobs show its rings).
Right-click: unlink knobs.
hz.synth_tip_macro_lamp: Lit while a macro turns a knob.
hz.synth_tab_mod_tip: MOD: more LFOs and envelopes, and the notes' velocity and pitch, to move knobs over time.
hz.synth_mod_hint: To link one of these to a knob, go to the OSC or FX tab and drag its name (in the strip at the top) onto the knob, as with a macro. Here, drag a box's name onto the other LFO's Rate to have it speed that LFO up and slow it down. Knobs that can't move don't light up.
hz.synth_tip_mod_lamp: Lit while this moves a knob.
hz.synth_mod_full: {n} links at most: remove one to add another.
hz.synth_tip_mod_add: Adds a link: LFO 3 on the first knob it doesn't move yet, at 50 %. Then pick its source and knob in the row.
hz.synth_tip_mod_col_source: What moves the knob: LFO 3 / 4, ENV 2 / 3 (set them above), Velocity (each note's loudness) or Note (how high each note is).
hz.synth_tip_mod_col_knob: The knob it moves. A source can move each knob once.
hz.synth_tip_mod_col_amount: How far it moves the knob at its top, in % of the knob's whole turn (below 0: the other way). Drag, wheel or type, as the knobs' boxes.
hz.synth_tip_mod_both: Both ways: the knob swings below and above where it's set (from -Amount to +Amount), instead of only going up from it.
hz.synth_tip_mod_remove: Remove this link (the knob stays where it's set).
hz.synth_tip_mod_name:
Drag this name onto a knob and hold it there until the knob lights up (half a second), then let go: it moves that knob over time. Only knobs that can move light up.
Click: pick it (the knobs show its rings; drag a ring to set how far).
Right-click: unlink knobs.
hz.synth_tip_mod_box_name:
Drag this name onto the other LFO's Rate and hold it there until the knob lights up (half a second), then let go: it speeds that LFO up and slows it down.
Click: pick it (the Rate knob shows its ring; drag the ring to set how far).
Right-click: unlink knobs.
hz.synth_tip_mod_lfo3: LFO 3: goes up and down over and over (set it on the MOD tab).
hz.synth_tip_mod_lfo4: LFO 4: goes up and down over and over (set it on the MOD tab).
hz.synth_tip_mod_env2: ENV 2: rises and falls once at each note (set it on the MOD tab).
hz.synth_tip_mod_env3: ENV 3: rises and falls once at each note (set it on the MOD tab).
hz.synth_tip_mod_velocity: Velocity: each note's own loudness (an Arpeggio step's Loudness; full otherwise).
hz.synth_tip_mod_note: Note: how high each note is (higher notes move the knob further).
hz.synth_tip_mod_shape: The LFO's shape over one wave.
hz.synth_tip_mod_mode: Free: runs on from the shape's start. Each note: starts over at each note. Once: one wave from each note's start, then stays at its end (like an envelope).
hz.synth_tip_mod_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the LFO goes round.
hz.synth_tip_mod_env: The envelope rises over Attack from each note's start, falls over Decay to Sustain, stays there while the note is held, and falls to 0 over Release after it. Times in beats.
hz.synth_tab_lines_tip: The effects' lines for one note, big: drag their points, as in the Hz bass window.
hz.synth_meter_tip: How many notes a second this sound makes while one {key} is held (its first 4 beats). A higher note makes more, a lower one fewer; Voices on Same keys, Echo, Reverb look-alike and Arpeggio add notes.
hz.rack_empty: No effects yet. Click one in the list on the left to put it on: Chorus, Flanger look-alike, Echo, Reverb look-alike or Compressor look-alike.
hz.rack_list_tip: Every effect. Click one to put it on the sound (lit: its strip shows on the right) or to take it off again. Drag one that's on up or down to change their order.
hz.rack_on_tip: Switches the effect off (or on again) without losing its knobs, to hear the sound without it.
hz.rack_reverb_notes: a fading tail after each note
hz.synth_tip_chorus_depth: Depth: how far out of tune every other key goes, in cents (100 = one key). A little sounds wide and moving.
hz.synth_tip_chorus_rate: Rate: how many times a beat it goes out of tune and back. 0 = no chorus.
hz.synth_tip_echo_time: Time: how long after the sound each repeat comes, in beats (0.75 = a dotted eighth).
hz.synth_tip_echo_repeats: Repeats: how many times the sound comes again. Each repeat is one more set of notes.
hz.synth_tip_echo_fade: Fade: how loud each repeat is, next to the one before it. 100 % = as loud, 0 = no repeats.
hz.synth_tip_reverb_length: Length: how long each note's tone rings on after the note ends, in beats.
hz.synth_tip_reverb_scatter: Scatter: how much the ringing tone's waves land out of place as it fades, like a room's echoes blurring together. 0 = it stays clean.
hz.synth_tip_reverb_level: Level: how loud the ringing starts, next to the note. It fades from there.
hz.synth_tip_flanger_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the moving keys go late and back. 0 = no flanger.
hz.synth_tip_flanger_depth: Depth: how late the moving keys get at most, as a share of one wave. More = a stronger sweep through the tone.
hz.synth_tip_flanger_mix: Mix: how many of the shape's keys move, spread evenly over them. 50 % = every other key, the strongest sweep. 100 % = every key moves together: only a slight wobble in pitch.
hz.synth_tip_compressor_threshold: Threshold: how loud the sound must be before it's turned down, in dB (0 = full). Lower = more of the sound is turned down.
hz.synth_tip_compressor_ratio: Ratio: how hard the loud parts are turned down. 4 : 1 = what's over the Threshold is cut to a quarter of how far over it was. 1 : 1 = not at all.
hz.synth_tip_compressor_attack: Attack: how long it takes to turn the sound down once it gets loud, in beats. A little lets each note's start through louder (punchier). 0 = at once.
hz.synth_tip_compressor_release: Release: how long it takes to stop turning the sound down once it gets quieter, in beats. Short = the quiet parts come up quickly (it can sound like pumping); long = smoother.
hz.synth_tip_compressor_gain: Gain: makes everything louder again afterwards, in dB, so the quiet parts come up next to the loud ones. Nothing gets louder than full.
hz.synth_tip_arp_swing: Swing: the notes between the steps of the beat grid (the 2nd, 4th… sixteenth at Speed 4) come a little late, for a bouncy, shuffled groove. 0 = even. 100 % = half a step late (the note before it gets longer, the late one shorter).
hz.synth_tip_steps: Your own steps, played in a loop. Click a name at the top to pick what you set: Note = which held note (1 = the lowest; if fewer are held, it counts round again; Rest = silence), Octave = up or down, Loudness, Length (times Gate; Tie at the top = it lasts on through the next step). Click or drag across the steps to set them. Middle-click a step = back to its start.
hz.synth_tip_steps_count: How many steps play (1 to 16). The steps past it are kept: make it bigger again and they come back.
hz.synth_tip_arp_scale: Scale: every note of the run is moved to the nearest note of this scale, so the Chord and Octaves never step outside the key. A note half way between two goes down. Off = the notes as they are.
hz.synth_tip_arp_root: Root: the note the Scale starts on (C major, A minor…). Does nothing while Scale is Off.
hz.synth_tip_arp_on: Click to switch the arpeggio on or off. On (lit): every note (or chord) you placed is played as a fast run of short notes instead. Turning one of its knobs or picking a Pattern or Chord switches it on too.
hz.synth_tip_lamp: Lit while this box changes the sound. Click it (or the box's name) to switch the box off: its knobs are kept, but it does nothing (bypass). Click again to switch it back on.
hz.synth_tip_arp_pattern: Pattern: the order of the run. Up = low to high, Down = high to low, Up and down = back and forth, Random = any order, Steps = your own steps (set in the grid under the picture).
hz.synth_tip_arp_chord: Chord: which notes the run goes through. Notes held = every note held at that step, as a synth's arpeggiator: a note added while the run goes joins it at its next step, a note let go drops out (a single note just goes through its Octaves). The others add that chord's notes to every note.
hz.synth_tip_arp_speed: Speed: how many notes a beat the run plays (4 = sixteenth notes).
hz.synth_tip_arp_octaves: Octaves: the run goes through its notes in this many octaves, one after the other. 1 = just the notes. With Steps: the steps are played again one octave higher each time round.
hz.synth_tip_arp_gate: Gate: how long each note of the run is, next to the time until the next one. 100 % = they touch (Glide can slide between them); less = short, plucky notes.
hz.synth_tip_blend: Blend: how loud the middle copy (the middle two, with an even number of Voices) is next to the outer ones. 50 % = all as loud. Lower = the middle louder, the outer ones fade (0 = only the middle). Higher = the outer ones louder, the middle fades (100 % = only the outer ones: wide and hollow). Needs 3 Voices or more. With Voices on Split keys each key row plays one copy, so Blend makes whole rows quieter (at 0 or 100 %, some rows go silent).
hz.synth_tip_random: Random start: each copy starts its wave at a random point at every new note, instead of all at the very start, so the notes don't all sound exactly alike and stacked Voices sound wider. 0 = every note starts the same. 100 % = anywhere in the wave. The same every time the notes are made.
hz.synth_tip_curve: Curve: how the Glide slides. Middle (0 %) = straight, at an even speed. Right = fast first, then settling into the note (the classic bass slide). Left = slow first, then rushing in. Starts at 50 %, as the glide always was.
hz.synth_tip_voices: Voices: how many copies of the sound play together, each a little out of tune with the others (Detune). They beat against each other: a thicker, wider sound. 1 = just the sound.
hz.synth_tip_detune: Detune: how far apart the highest and the lowest copy are, in cents (100 cents = one key). The others are spread evenly between them. A little (10-30) sounds thick, a lot sounds out of tune.
hz.synth_tip_voices_on: Voices on: Split keys = the shape's keys take turns playing the copies, one copy each (no extra notes). Same keys = every key plays every copy, so the copies drift in and out of each other (as many times the notes as there are voices).
hz.synth_tip_glide: Glide: each note slides in from the tone of the note before it, taking this long. 0 = no glide. Each note still starts its own envelope. No glide from a note of the same tone, or into a note a slide you made reaches.
hz.synth_tip_cc:
Where the MIDI CC lines (Effects pane, under "MIDI CC") go.

One channel: the whole Hz bass shares its channel, so every note hears the same values.

Own channel per note: each note gets a channel of its own with its own values, so a line played once per note starts again with each note. Chords no longer merge into one line of notes. A note keeps its channel until its sound and the lines' run-on have ended. Needs Multi channel.

Past 15 channels the MIDI file uses ports: in a MIDI editor or player, give every port a device. Without CC lines this changes nothing.
hz.synth_tip_legato: A note that starts right where another ends carries on from it, as one long note: the envelopes don't start over (no new Attack), and the first note doesn't fade out (no Release) until the last one ends. With the Arpeggio at Gate 100 %, the whole run gets one envelope. Notes with a gap between them still start over.
hz.synth_tip_touching: Only notes that touch: a note glides only when it starts right where the note before it ends. Off = it glides even after a gap.
hz.synth_tip_sweep: Sweep: one part of the shape's keys is loud and the others get quieter, and that part can move while the note sounds. Turning one of its knobs ticks On too.
hz.synth_tip_sweep_start: Start: where the loud part is when a note starts. 0 % = the lowest keys, 100 % = the highest.
hz.synth_tip_sweep_end: End: where it moves to. The same as Start = it stays still.
hz.synth_tip_sweep_time: Time: how long it takes to move from Start to End after each note starts. 0 = it stays at Start.
hz.synth_tip_sweep_track: Key track: how far the loud part moves with each note's pitch. At 100 % it moves one key row up for every key the note is above the Hz bass's own tone (and down for notes below it), so higher notes sound brighter, like a filter following the keyboard. Below 0 = the other way. 0 = every note the same.
hz.synth_tip_wah: Wah: loud and quiet stripes over the keys, more stripes the more it's turned. 0 = every key full. Strongest together with Slant.
hz.synth_tip_slant: Slant: every key starts a little later than the key below it. 100 % = spread over one whole wave. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_groups: Groups: the keys take turns in this many groups. 1 = all together. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_offpitch: Off pitch: every key repeats a little slower or faster than the tone, so the keys drift apart and meet again by themselves. 100 % = 2 % between the lowest and the highest key.
hz.preset_tip: Presets: ready-made sounds. Click to pick one: ours first, then the ones you saved. A * after the name means the sound has been changed since it was picked. A preset is the whole sound (every knob and line), not the notes or their Note length.
hz.preset_save_tip: Keep this sound as a preset of your own (every knob and line, not the notes).
hz.preset_save_prompt: Name of the preset (the same name as one of yours replaces it):
hz.preset_name_taken: "{name}" is one of the presets that come with Spiderweb. Pick another name:
hz.preset_delete_tip: Delete this preset of yours (the ones that come with Spiderweb can't be deleted).
hz.preset_delete_ask: Delete the preset "{name}"? The sound you have now stays as it is.
hz.preset_file_broken:
The file with your presets couldn't be read (it's damaged), so a new one is started. The old one was kept as:
{path}
hz.synth_tip_noisy: Noisy: every repeat is late by a random bit. 100 % = up to one whole wave.
hz.synth_tip_height: Height: the drawn wave shape (Hz shape…) gets taller or shorter. 100 % = as drawn (the knob's middle). Lower = the keys it no longer reaches go quiet. Higher, up to 400 % = it grows past the Hz bass onto the keys above and below. Link an LFO on the MOD tab to make it grow and shrink over and over.
hz.synth_tip_height_rand: Random height: every wave gets its own height, a random bit taller or shorter than Height says (the same for all keys). 100 % = anywhere from flat to twice as tall, but never past 400 %.
hz.synth_tip_height_from: Grows from: the key row that stays put while Height changes. Middle = grows and shrinks both ways, Bottom = only upwards, Top = only downwards.
hz.synth_tip_vibrato_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the tone goes up and down.
hz.synth_tip_vibrato_depth: Depth: how far the tone goes up and down. 100 % = almost a key each way. 0 = no vibrato.
hz.synth_tip_vibrato_delay: Rise: after the Delay, the vibrato grows from nothing to its full Depth over this long, as many singers and synths do. 0 = full at once.
hz.synth_tip_tremolo_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the sound gets quieter and louder again. 0 = no tremolo.
hz.synth_tip_tremolo_depth: Depth: how much quieter it gets. 100 % = down to silence.
hz.synth_tip_wave: Waveform: the shape of each wave. Plain = one note a wave, the brightest sound. Sine = the softest, darkest sound. Square, Triangle and Saw are in between, each with its own colour. A waveform makes up to 16 notes a wave instead of one: the picture below shows them.
hz.synth_tip_shape: Shape: how much of the waveform is used. 0 % = the plain tone, 100 % = the whole waveform (more notes).
hz.synth_tip_octave: Octave below: every other wave gets softer, so the tone an octave lower comes in (like a synth's sub oscillator). No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_amount: Amount: how many keys up (or down, turned left) each note starts, before it glides to its own tone. 0 = no glide.
hz.synth_tip_time: Time: how long that glide takes.
hz.synth_tip_bend_range: Range: how many keys the Pitch line bends at its top (and down at its bottom), 1 to 48. Turning it keeps the line as it is, so the whole bend gets bigger or smaller, like a synth's pitch bend range. Big upward bends make the notes' gates shorter. Macros can't turn it.
hz.synth_tip_cutoff: Cutoff: how bright the sound is. Sent as MIDI CC 74 (the Cutoff line in the Effects pane), so the player's soundfont does the filtering: some soundfonts don't react to it. 50 % = where players start (nothing sent). Other shapes on the same channel hear it too.
hz.synth_tip_filter_amount: Amount: how far the envelope moves the Cutoff at each note. Up = brighter, down = darker. 0 = the Cutoff stays put.
hz.synth_tip_filter_attack: Attack: how long the Cutoff takes to move the whole Amount after a note starts.
hz.synth_tip_filter_decay: Decay: how long it then takes to come back to the Sustain level.
hz.synth_tip_filter_sustain: Sustain: how much of the Amount stays while the note is held.
hz.synth_tip_filter_release: Release: how long the Cutoff takes to go back after the note ends.
hz.synth_tip_attack: Attack: how long the sound takes to get loud after you press a key.
hz.synth_tip_decay: Decay: how long it then takes to drop to the Sustain level.
hz.synth_tip_sustain: Sustain: how loud it stays while you hold the key. Above about 50 % it sounds almost the same; changes are easiest to hear in the quiet part.
hz.synth_tip_release: Release: how long it takes to fade out after you let go of the key.
hz.synth_tip_knob: Drag up / down (Shift = fine), mouse wheel or arrow keys. Right mouse button: points it at the mouse. Middle-click = back to the start. Or type a value in the box under it (a letter that plays a key takes it at once; to multiply, type * not x). Linked to a macro: drag its coloured ring to set how far the macro turns it (down to 0 = unlinked).
hz.synth_drawn: Its lines were drawn by hand (Draw tab), so the knobs only show about where they are. Turning one makes new lines from the knobs.
hz.live_recording: Live keys: recording notes from the soundfont…
hz.live_playing: Live keys: a quick copy, not your MIDI ({mb} MB kept)
hz.live_rough: Live keys: a rough copy, not your MIDI: too many different notes, so every {n} keys play together ({mb} MB kept)
